first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_31, memory_86) plus a supporting one (memory_91) point to onboarding/activation-focused interventions producing durable, non-harmful lifts. The competitor's aggressive pricing move creates pressure to respond with promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly warns that this tactic, despite acquisition gains, materially damages 30-day retention and was flagged as not generalizable — a clear downstream value risk given our objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term acquisition. I want to verify memory_73's original record to confirm the retention harm is robust enough to justify avoiding the reactive pricing response, and verify memory_86 (the most directly relevant, more recent memory on onboarding completion) before committing our single experiment slot to simplify_onboarding. This action directly targets the two metrics currently declining, has multiple corroborating memories, and avoids the flagged retention risk of promotional pricing. I'm running it as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout to preserve calibration, since current conditions (competitive pricing pressure) differ somewhat from when memory_86/memory_31 were originally observed.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both prior assessments: exp_73 shows promotional pricing drives +18% qualified revenue and +31% signups short-term, but -12% 30-day retention with the acquired cohort not surviving first renewal — this directly undermines sustainable long-term qualified revenue, our stated objective, despite competitive pressure from the entrant's pricing move. Reacting to a competitor with a tactic we've already proven self-destructive would be repeating a known mistake under new framing. Exp_86 confirms shortened onboarding improves completion (+13%), time-to-value, and even retention (+3%), with no negative side effects noted, directly addressing our current onboarding completion decline. Combined with memory_31 (signup simplification lifting activation) and memory_91 (activation messaging improving engagement), onboarding/activation intervention is the best-supported, lowest-risk use of this week's single experiment slot, directly targeting both metrics currently in decline (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%). I'm keeping it at standard_experiment scale rather than broad_rollout since current market conditions (aggressive competitor pricing) differ from the original test environment, and I want to confirm the lift still holds before scaling further. I'm not recommending promotional_pricing at any scale given the confirmed retention damage, and I'm flagging that ignoring competitor pricing pressure entirely carries its own risk that should be monitored even though it's not this week's experiment.
